title: MemOS — paper view
subtitle: The mechanism as Li et al. describe it. The A/B split below is an alignment device only — Figure 8 draws write and retrieve as one closed loop within a single turn. Empty/degraded lanes mean the paper leaves that step optional or undefined.
source: Li et al. 2025, MemOS (arXiv:2507.03724v4)   ·   every anchor re-located in the paper text during verification (40 paper-side assertions, 31 ✓ / 9 ◐ / 0 ✗)
legend_notes: Write and retrieve are not sequential here: W1 and R1 are the SAME MemReader call, packaging one MemoryCall that feeds both extraction and retrieval intent — the A/B split is drawn only for cross-system alignment (call / call_query share seq 2).

A6 INTERNALIZE (Convert:Plaintext→Activation / →Parametric) is P-TRANSMUTE, the primitive minted for this system's headline claim — and every trigger condition (when, how much, at what cost) is left unstated by the paper, hence degraded styling through A4/A6/B3/B6.

B5 SELECT fires before the B4 rerank score exists: MemoryPathResolver's scope/order planning (route_select) precedes the 4-metric scoring (rerank) in the paper's own sequence — the opposite of the usual score-then-select order.
B8 LOOP is empty on purpose: no multi-hop, iterative retrieval, or agent tool loop is described anywhere in the text.
